Definition: from G820; used like G818, to maltreat:--handle shamefully.
BiblicalUsage: This word means to handle shamefully, and it appears in the parable of the vineyard, where the tenants wounded the owner's servant in the head and sent him away shamefully handled. It stands in the Textus Receptus at this verse, where other Greek texts read the related word for dishonour.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that the tenants' shameful handling of the servant shows what rebellion does to every messenger God sends, and the parable ends with the stone the builders rejected.
